title: Name your project and check free domains with agents
summary: A student built six Gemma-powered agents that read a repo, suggest names and check domains; after seven chat rounds it renamed itself NameMatch with a free .tech domain.
agent_role: A supervisor agent reads the project and picks namers; three namer agents propose names; a checker suggests variants for taken domains; a feedback agent revises names from the user's chat.
outcome: Author reports a naming round dropped from 8-10 minutes to 2-5 after turning off model thinking, and the app renamed itself in seven rounds.
what_they_did: A developer who struggles with naming built a team of six AI agents. You paste a GitHub link or a text file and answer a few questions. The agents read the project, suggest names, check if .com, .dev, .app, .tech or .ai domains are free, and refine names as you chat.
how_it_went: They say one naming round fell from 8-10 minutes to 2-5 after turning off the model's extra thinking on simpler steps. Run on its own code, it produced NameMatch after seven rounds.
worth_knowing: Turning thinking off cut one namer call from 79 seconds to 5, but doing so on the final pick let weaker names through. Free model tiers also hit rate limits.
prompt: Read the project at [repo URL or README]. Summarise what it does and who it's for, then suggest 10 names in three styles: professional, short, and playful. For each, check whether [preferred domain endings, e.g. .com, .dev] are available and list only names with a free domain. Ask me which direction I like and refine over several rounds. Don't register or buy anything.

curation.rationale: Working multi-agent tool with open code, concrete timing numbers, and a real use (renaming itself); a modest but fun application.
